deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the construction, begun on the previous page, of a canonical resolution of a module on the infinitesimal or crystalline site of X/S. The setting is Grothendieck's late-1966/1967 work on crystals and de Rham cohomology.

**The resolution.** Let X^{[i]} denote the (i+1)-fold fibre product of X over S, formally completed along the diagonal. That is, it is the i-th term of the cosimplicial 'nerve' of X in the site. Write P^i_{(n)} for the sheaves of principal parts of order n on X^{[i]}, and set
- Q^i_{(n)} = P^i_{(n)};
- Q^i[M]_{(n)} = Q^i_{(n)} ⊗_{O_X} M;
- Q^i[M] = lim_n Q^i[M]_{(n)}, a pro-module.

Applying the linearization functor ℓ (Berthelot's L) gives a cosimplicial, hence cochain, object ℓQ^*[M]. In good cases (M quasi-coherent) it resolves M.

**Consequences.**
- H^*(X,M) ≅ ℍ^*(X, ℓQ^*[M]).
- The hypercohomology spectral sequence of the cochain complex is E_2^{pq} = H^p(i ↦ H^q(X, ℓQ^i[M])) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X,M).
- Under suitable conditions H^q(X, ℓQ^i[M]) = lim_n H^q(X, Q^i[M]_{(n)}). This is the Zariski cohomology of M on the completed product X^{[i+1]}^, where X^{[i+1]} = [X/S]^{i+2} in the new indexing. The original line read H^q(X^{[i]}, M), and it was struck out.
- The marginal note ('Mention +1 comme ∧!') is a reminder of an index shift by one.

This is the Čech–Alexander computation of infinitesimal or crystalline cohomology.

**Complexes.** Next the construction is extended to a bounded-below complex M^· in D^+(Mod(X/S)) = D^+(X/S). One gets a bicomplex Q^*[M^·] whose linearization resolves M^·. Hence
H^*(X,M^·) ≅ ℍ^*(X, Q^*[M^·]) ≅ ℍ^*(X_Zar, Q^0[M^·]).
The final remark interprets Q^0[M^·] as the 'formalization' (formal completion) of complexes of differential operators. This is the dictionary between complexes of differential operators on X and complexes of linearized (pro-)modules or crystals.

**Purpose.** The page serves the comparison of infinitesimal/crystalline cohomology with Zariski (de Rham-type) cohomology. It was preparatory to the Nov–Dec 1967 IHES lectures ('Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes').
errors: The indexing of X^{[i]} versus X^{[i+1]} = [X/S]^{i+2} is inconsistent. Grothendieck himself corrects it in the margin and by the strikeout, but the 'i+1 facteurs' remark sits awkwardly with the exponent i+2.
In the last displayed line the left side is written H^*(X,M); for consistency with the complex case it should be ℍ^*(X,M^·).

'Under suitable conditions' is not specified. The Mittag-Leffler/lim^1 conditions needed to pass H^q through lim_n, and the question raised on the previous page (whether AR-pro-modules form an abelian category), are left open.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial resolution Q^*[M] = (principal parts on iterated formal diagonal products) ⊗ M, linearized, resolving M on the infinitesimal/crystalline site
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés (1968)

ideas.what: Spectral sequence E_2^{pq}=H^p(i↦H^q(X,ℓQ^i[M])) and identification of terms with cohomology of completed products X^{[i+1]}^
ideas.modern_name: Čech-to-derived spectral sequence for the infinitesimal site
ideas.where_published: Crystals paper, Čech computation of infinitesimal cohomology

ideas.what: Extension to complexes in D^+(X/S) via a bicomplex; Zariski hypercohomology of Q^0[M^·] interpreted as formalized complexes of differential operators
ideas.modern_name: Linearization of differential operators (complexes of differential operators ↔ crystal complexes)
ideas.where_published: Crystals paper (linearization of differential operators); Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline, LNM 407

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard working notes for the 1967 IHES crystals lectures. Everything on the page (Čech–Alexander resolution, linearization, the comparison spectral sequence, complexes of differential operators) appears in the published Crystals paper and in Berthelot's work.
transcription_corrections: The subscript transcribed 'κ' in Q^i_κ[M]_{(n)} and X^{[i+1]}_κ is probably a mark (a star or an indexing symbol), not a kappa.
The final line should read 'Q^0[M^·] s'interprète comme la formalisation des complexes d'op. différentiels M^·'.
Last formula: 'H^*(X_Zar, Q^0[M^·])' (square brackets), consistent with the notation elsewhere.
Before 'complexe M^·': 'Si on a un complexe M^·'; the word after M^· is likely 'borné inférieurement' or similar, given D^+.
Before 'résolution de M^·': 'soit une résolution de M^·, et par suite'.
